content.comment_body: I need to set up communication between a [product_name] and a [version_no]. I'm using the [product_name] module with Ethernet interface ([article_no]). What I want is to read inputs from the [product_name] and write the bits into a DB on the [version_no], without sending anything from the [version_no] back to the [product_name]. Is this possible?

This is not an issue, as you can transfer data from the [version_no] to the [product_name] too. Data exchange works in both directions. It's important to decide which device acts as server or client since both can fulfill either role. If the [product_name] is the server, programming on the [version_no] gets more complex, requiring a PUT / GET function for data exchange. It's easier if the [version_no] is the server. I have sample programs for both scenarios, but they're in German; let me know if you'd like me to upload them.
Good morning! I would like to receive a demonstration of a configuration where the [version_no] acts as master to a [product_name]. Greetings!
Hello [user_name], Please note this forum operates in English. Kindly post your questions in English to receive support. Best regards, [user_name] Support

Hello [user_name], Welcome to the forum. This is an English-speaking space, so please write future posts in English. Thanks. Attached is an example for communication setup: [product_name] as client, [version_no] as server.
Attached is an example for how to set up communication with [product_name] as server and [version_no] as client.
